stem:
Pihu compares the Sun with other stars on a clear evening chart. The Sun looks large and bright by day. Other stars look like tiny points at night and are not seen in the daytime sky.

Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The Sun is the star closest to Earth, so it appears much larger and brighter than farther stars.
Every star equally powerful looks equally bright from Earth at any distance.
An identical star farther from Earth appears larger and brighter than a nearer one.
The Sun appears as a tiny point from Earth, just like every other star.

teacher.key_rationale: The Sun is the nearest star, so it looks large and bright. Distance matters for brightness and size on the sky; reversing nearer/farther or treating the Sun as a tiny point are wrong.
